changes: Viṭṭhala→Sadāśiva relation kept as son_of, but 'sadāśivātmaja sutasya(!)' could also mean 'son of Sadāśiva's son' (grandson); the possibility is now in the notes and Sadāśiva's confidence is lowered to medium
Purpose changed from 'śrīkṛṣṇārpaṇa' to a description: a pious dedication to Kṛṣṇa, not a statement of who the copy was for
Notes now say that '|| 68 ||' is a verse or section number, not a date, and that 'svahastaṃ' only means the scribe wrote it in his own hand

notes: Two scribes wrote different parts of this composite manuscript: Viṭṭhala wrote the Aduḥkhanavamīvratakathā (exp. 19t) and Śivarāma wrote the udyāpana section (exp. 24b). This matches the catalogue. Viṭṭhala's colophon is corrupt in 'sadāśivātmaja sutasya(!)'. It most likely means 'Viṭṭhala, son of Sadāśiva, of the Parāḍkara family'. It could also be read as 'Viṭṭhala, son of the son of Sadāśiva', which would make him Sadāśiva's grandson. 'Parāḍkara' (a Marathi-type surname, upanāma) is recorded as the family affiliation. '|| 68 ||' is a verse or section count, not a date. The manuscript is undated. 'svahastaṃ' means only that Viṭṭhala wrote it in his own hand; it is not a statement of ownership.
